name: cut_shortens_the_bar
why: ENTRY Z-C6. `trim_members` was in the catalogue with `Tested = true` and no case touched it. When the case was written, on 25/9/2026, it turned out that **it had never cut anything**: it passed the bodies as `object[]`, SOLIDWORKS answered with a «Trim/Extend1» feature that did not enter the tree, and the operation said `bodies_trimmed: 1` on a part identical to before. With `Body2[]` the cut is born.
defect_caught: Two, and they are the same lie seen from both sides. Step 5 catches the cut that does not cut: the T must lose exactly the 40 mm by which the short bar enters the long one, and a phantom cut would leave the volume as it was. Step 4 catches the guard that does not bite: between two parallel bars that do not meet SOLIDWORKS STILL answers with the phantom feature — even with the typed arrays — and the operation must say so instead of confirming.
_and_the_twin_is_in_the_same_file: The refusal (step 4) and the good cut (step 5) differ by one argument only: WHICH bar is cut against the long one. The far one does not meet it, the short one does.
_the_bodies_are_called_by_name: The bodies are called by name. Not C1, C2, C3: with these three bars, created in the same order, the state once said C1 = the short one and another time C1 = the long one (measured on 25/9/2026, two runs). The name — «(1)», «(2)», «(3)» — follows the order of creation, and it is what the case means: (1) the long one, (2) the short one, (3) the far one. It is really needed: by symmetry the NOTCH of the long one against the short one removes exactly the same volume as the cut of the short one (40 mm of half tube by 80), so with the bodies swapped step 5 would stay green while working on the wrong bar.

expect.why: the short one starts from the AXIS of the long one: it goes into it by half a width, 40 mm

expect.tolerance_why: 1500 mm of 80x80x5 tube at 1469.956 mm2 of section: the section has the corner radii, so pi inside. Half a mm3 out of two million covers the rounding; one bar fewer or more shifts the volume by hundreds of thousands

40 mm x 1469.956 mm2 = 58798.23: the 40 mm by which the short one entered the long one. The section has pi inside (the radii), so the calculation is to the hundredth and not exact. A phantom cut would give 0
2204933.61 minus 58798.23. Read from the part, not from the operation: it is the second reading of the same fact
